# Stock Market Today (July 23, 2026): Sensex, Nifty Open Lower As US-Iran Escalation, Oil Price Spike Weigh On S
*By Sakshi Bajaj*
---
[Markets](https://www.timesnownews.com/business-economy/markets)
-   Authored by: [Sakshi Bajaj](https://www.timesnownews.com/author/sakshi-bajaj-479252376)
-   Updated Jul 23, 2026, 09:24 IST
## GIFT Nifty futures indicated a negative start to the trading session on Thursday as investors tracked the escalating US-Iran conflict.
![Stock Market Today (July 23, 2026)](https://images.timesnownews.com/thumb/msid-155153914,thumbsize-52736,width-1280,height-720,resizemode-75/155153914.jpg)
Stock Market Today (July 23, 2026)
Photo :
iStock
Both the Nifty and the Sensex began the trading day on a weak note on July 23, 2026. Investors continued to monitor the fresh escalation in the US-Iran conflict and the 6-week high spike in crude oil prices. The Nifty and Sensex declined 0.4 percent at open. The Nifty declined nearly 100 points and opened at 23,904.80 and the Sensex declined over 300 points and opened at 76,515.10. The Indian rupee opened at 96.49 to the dollar versus Wednesday's close of 96.57 to the dollar. Most sectoral indices traded in the red in early trade.
G. Chokkalingam Head of Research at Equinomics Research told Times Now Digital, "[continued conflicts](https://www.timesnownews.com/world/middle-east/our-defence-doctrine-is-clear-irans-eye-for-an-eye-warning-as-us-assault-enters-12th-night-article-155153672) and subsequent rally in crude oil prices is a cause of worry. Oil has now moved up over 18% in the last couple of weeks. Due to rally in oil prices, the rupee is also likely to remain weak today. Therefore equity markets are likely to remain weak today. However, by the end of this week global political pressures should start building up to reduce conflicts. Hope still remains as continued conflicts in West Asia will cause severe economic crisis for Iran and significant economic pressures for all major economies including US and China. Hence investors focusing on quality small and midcap companies, which focus largely on domestic demand themes will do well in the short-term to medium-term. Largecaps especially Sensex & Nifty basket stocks generally may come under pressures due to continued FII selling."
Crude oil prices hit a fresh 6-week high, Brent Crude Oil rates spiked 2 percent and crossed 96 dollars per barrel and WTI Crude Oil surpassed 88 dollars per barrel following the [fresh escalation](https://www.timesnownews.com/world/us/us-news/more-troops-more-medics-more-weapons-trump-boosts-up-us-military-build-up-in-middle-east-as-iran-war-deepens-article-155153529) in the US-Iran conflict. Stock markets plunged on Wednesday. The Sensex declined 715.06 points and ended the trading day at 76,755.05 and the Nifty declined 191.45 points and closed at 23,996.25.
